title: The Woman Who Accidentally Became a Queen for One Day
sources: Historical folklore & village monarch misidentification records
Princess Caraboo and regional monarch-for-a-day carnival traditions

lines.text: She went to buy a loaf of bread,
and by lunchtime, an entire village was bowing at her feet.
See, in eighteen eighty-eight, a town telegram warned that the Queen
lines.caps: in 1888, | a telegram | warned | the Queen

lines.text: was traveling in disguise, wearing a blue polka-dot apron.
Enter Clara, clutching fresh warm sourdough,
in the exact same polka-dot apron.
The second she stepped outside, the mayor fell to his knees.
and before Clara could speak, they threw a velvet cape over her shoulders
and slapped an antique gold crown on her head.
Her first royal decree: free pastries for every kid,
and mandatory afternoon naps for the adults.
When the real Queen finally arrived,
she took one bite of the free pastries, laughed, and let Clara keep the crown.
So next time you go to buy bread,
bring a basket, just in case you inherit a throne.
